procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and order dated February 3, 1964, in Writ Petition No. 201 of 1963, given in a batch of Writ Petitions.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: A batch of Writ Petitions challenged the Andhra Pradesh Amendment Act (related to state carriages) in the High Court. The High Court initially struck down the Act as unconstitutional. Later, after Act 34 of 1961 was passed to validate the levy and impose a surcharge, the operators again questioned the Amendment Act. The High Court rejected the Writ Petitions but directed that the respondents (presumably the Regional Transport Authority) could not collect the enhanced surcharge for May 1959.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appeal to the Supreme Court is by a Certificate against the Judgment of the Andhra Pradesh High Court. The appellants are K. Mangachari, K. R. Chaudhuri and K. Rajendra Cltdudhury.

issue.issue_text: Whether there is an impediment for motor vehicle operators to collect enhanced fares without a formal amendment to the conditions of their permit, following a government notification fixing maximum fares.

facts: The government of Andhra Pradesh imposed an enhanced surcharge on motor vehicle operators.
To allow operators to recover this cost, the government issued a notification (G.O. Ms. No. 1077) under Section 43 of the Motor Vehicles Act, authorizing the fixing of new, higher maximum fares.
The transport authorities then notified the operators, authorizing them to collect these enhanced fares.

The operators (appellants) argued that they could not legally collect the higher fares because the specific fare tables attached to their individual permits had not been formally and physically amended.
They feared that collecting fares higher than those listed in their permits would be a violation that could lead to the cancellation of their permits.
law: Section 43(1)(i) of the Motor Vehicles Act grants the government the power to issue notifications fixing maximum or minimum fares for stage carriages.
Section 59(3)(c) of the Motor Vehicles Act states that it is a condition of every permit that any maximum fares fixed by a notification under Section 43 must be observed.
application: The Court determined that the government's notification fixing the maximum fares was a valid exercise of its power under Section 43(1)(i).

The Court then reasoned that Section 59(3)(c) operates automatically. Once a notification is issued under Section 43, Section 59(3)(c) has the immediate legal effect of incorporating the new maximum fares as a condition of the permit.
This means the permit conditions are considered "statutorily amended" by the notification itself, without the need for a separate, physical alteration of each individual permit.
The Court held that the notification, followed by the directions from the transport authorities, was sufficient authorization for the operators to collect the enhanced fares.
Therefore, the operators' fear that collecting the new fares would lead to the cancellation of their permits was unjustified.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court rejected the operators' argument, concluding that there was no impediment to collecting the enhanced fares. The government's notification under Section 43, combined with the automatic effect of Section 59(3)(c), legally and statutorily amended the conditions of their permits, making a formal, physical amendment unnecessary.

issue.issue_text: Whether the payment of the enhanced tax by operators is dependent on them actually collecting the enhanced fares from passengers.

reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court explicitly chose not to answer this question. The judgment states, "There is of course the other basic question whether the payment of the enhanced tax is dependent on the operators collecting the enhanced fares. In any case it is unnecessary to consider this .question in the view we have taken that the contention urged by the Appellant is unsustainable." The Court found that the operators were legally authorized to collect the enhanced fares, which made their primary argument invalid. Because their main contention failed, the Court did not need to address the separate, underlying issue of whether the tax payment was dependent on fare collection.

arguments.issue_text: Whether there is an impediment for motor vehicle operators to collect enhanced fares without a formal amendment to the conditions of their permit, following a government notification fixing maximum fares.
appellant_arguments: Unless the table of fares attached to their permit is formally altered in accordance with procedure, they cannot lawfully collect the enhanced fares which include the new tax.
Collecting the enhanced fares without a formal amendment to the permit could lead to the cancellation of their permits.
Relying on the Madhya Pradesh Transport Co. case, a formal revision of fare tables is necessary to enable operators to recover the tax amount from passengers.
respondent_arguments: The government notification issued under Section 43 of the Motor Vehicles Act, authorizing the collection of enhanced fares, is sufficient authorization.
By virtue of Section 59(3)(c) of the Act, the government notification statutorily and automatically amends the conditions of the permit, incorporating the new maximum fares.
No separate, physical amendment to the fare tables in each permit is required.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the payment of the enhanced tax by operators is dependent on them actually collecting the enhanced fares from passengers.
appellant_arguments: The obligation to pay the enhanced tax is dependent on the legal ability to collect the corresponding enhanced fares from passengers.
respondent_arguments: The text does not contain the respondent's arguments on this specific issue.
arguments.court_acceptance: The court did not answer this question, deeming it unnecessary in light of its decision on the first issue.

cases.case_name: Nazeeria Motor Service etc. etc. v. State of Andhra Pradesh & Anr.
cases.principle: The constitutionality of the surcharge had already been upheld.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: Once a government notification is issued under Section 43(1)(i) of the Motor Vehicles Act setting maximum fares, the conditions of a permit are statutorily amended by virtue of Section 59(3)(c), and it has the effect of incorporating the notified maximum fares, including any tax leviable, as a condition of the permit. A separate amendment of the fare table is not required for an operator to lawfully collect the enhanced fares.
obiter: The question of whether the payment of an enhanced tax by an operator is dependent on the operator collecting the enhanced fares from passengers is not considered.
A case where no notification was issued under Section 43 is not an authority for the proposition that a fare table must be altered before an enhanced surcharge can be collected.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court concluded that a government notification issued under Section 43 of the Motor Vehicles Act, which fixes maximum fares, automatically and statutorily amends the conditions of an operator's permit by virtue of Section 59(3)(c) of the Act. This statutory amendment has the effect of incorporating the new maximum fares as a condition of the permit, thereby legally authorizing operators to collect the enhanced fares without needing a separate, physical alteration to the table of fares attached to their individual permits.
legal_tests_applied: Statutory Interpretation of the Motor Vehicles Act, specifically the interplay between Section 43(1)(i) and Section 59(3)(c), to determine if a government notification can automatically amend a permit's conditions.
why_appellant_lost: The court held that once a notification is issued by the government under Section 43(1)(i), Section 59(3)(c) comes into play and has the effect of statutorily incorporating the new maximum fares as a condition of the permit, negating the need for a formal amendment.

The appellant's fear that collecting enhanced fares would lead to permit cancellation was dismissed as having no justification, given that the permit conditions were deemed legally amended by the statute itself.

The precedent cited by the appellant, the Madhya Pradesh Transport Co. case, was distinguished as not being applicable because it did not involve a notification under Section 43, nor did that court consider the provisions of Section 59(3)(c).
why_respondent_won: The court accepted the argument that the government notification under Section 43 was sufficient authorization for operators to collect the enhanced fares.

The court's reasoning was that Section 59(3)(c) of the Act causes the conditions of the permit to be statutorily and automatically amended to reflect the new maximum fares set by the government's notification.
